name: fenced-lease
description: Profile B's reference owner: a reaped or superseded owner's token is refused, and a READY row has no owner.

actions.init: A fresh InMemoryOwner and one claimable row
actions.claim: InMemoryOwner.claim(); the returned token is remembered as the last issued
actions.write: InMemoryOwner.fenced_write(row, token) with the last or previous issued token
actions.retry: InMemoryOwner.fenced_retry(row, token) with the last or previous issued token
actions.release: InMemoryOwner.release_unchanged(row, token) with the last or previous issued token
actions.renew: InMemoryOwner.renew_lease(row, token) with the last or previous issued token

mutants.name: shipped-9aa6ff2
mutants.description: The exact InMemoryOwner re-arm methods shipped at 9aa6ff2, before the fix: the row returns to READY but keeps the previous owner's token, which can still write or renew it

mutants.name: reaper-ignores-lease
mutants.description: The reaper re-arms any claimed row, taking it from an owner whose lease is still live

mutants.name: unfenced-renewal
mutants.description: renew_lease ignores the token, so a dead owner can keep a lease alive

bugs_found.summary: Profile B's reference owner kept a reaped owner's token valid until the next claim, so that owner could still renew a READY row or write it to RETRYABLE, where no claim or reaper reaches it; the profile's stale-token proofs never tried the token in that window
bugs_found.found_by: a state-machine audit of the references, confirmed by replaying claim, expire, reclaim and a late write against the real InMemoryOwner

limits: One row and the reference's own clock, which never advances; lease state is read as none, live or expired from the deadline.
Tokens are named by age (last or previous issued); a never-issued token stands in when there is no such token.
This contracts the reference owner the profile B proofs are calibrated against, not an adopter's binding; adopters are judged by the proofs in bounded_ownership.py.
shipped-9aa6ff2 runs history/rearm-9aa6ff2.py.txt, the three pre-fix methods copied verbatim from 9aa6ff2 and pinned by SHA-256 in conftest.py.
